subject: Order Form: pricing stitch, invoice entity mapping & net-terms proposal

Subject: Order Form: pricing stitch, invoice entity mapping & net-terms proposal

Hi Bradley / Anita —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a redline of the Order Form (Medivex_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf) and the proposed Pricing Schedule spreadsheet. The two items I want to align on before we send this to Legal / Procurement are:

1) Invoice entity mapping — Medivex requested invoices to route to a single US parent (Medivex Holdings) while operational charges should map to the local operating entity for tax purposes. We can support that but need your confirmation about which legal entity will be responsible for payment on each line item.

2) Net terms — your procurement team mentioned Net45 as a preference. The MSA lists Net30; if the Order Form is meant to override that please confirm so we can reflect it explicitly.

Proposal (quick):
- Activation & one-time onboarding fees invoiced to Medivex Holdings on execution.
- Monthly subscription invoices billed to Operating Entity A (for services consumed) with invoice copies to Medivex Holdings.
- Net45 on recurring invoices for enterprise customers; activation fee remains due Net30.
- Taxes: operating entity handles VAT/GST withholding; Redwood will include a withholding fallback clause (see redline). Customer to provide VAT registration evidence to avoid reverse-charge confusion.

Can you confirm by EOD Friday whether: (a) Medivex Holdings accepts primary invoicing for activation fees, and (b) Net45 is acceptable for recurring invoices? If yes we’ll incorporate your confirmation into a clean Order Form and route to DocuSign.

Attachments: Medivex_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf, PricingSchedule_Medivex_v2.xlsx

Best,
Naomi Feldman

- Net45 is our standard for new vendors; we can make Net45 work but we need an SLA credit if invoices go beyond 60 days (internal policy).

Appreciate the quick confirm, Bradley. Based on your note we’ll update the Order Form as follows:

- Invoice routing: Activation fee -> Medivex Holdings (Entity A). Recurring subscription -> Medivex Health Solutions LLC (Entity B).
- Net terms: Recurring invoices Net45; activation fee Net30. We will add an SLA credit for late payments beyond 60 days (proposed 5% credit on next invoice) — suggest we put that in the billing appendix.
- Taxes: We’ll add a short clause: "Customer's operating entity is responsible for local VAT/GST; Redwood will invoice gross and provide tax-ready invoices. Any withholding taxes will be grossed-up or subject to documented evidence per Appendix B." Please confirm if that phrasing works.

I attached a cleaned Order Form that reflects these changes and highlights the exact clause language (Attachment: Medivex_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf — see pages 4/5). If you can confirm the entity names and upload the VAT docs, we’ll route to Legal and then DocuSign.

- Bradley / Anita: confirm the exact legal names and attach VAT evidence (W-8/W-9 as applicable).
- Oliver: once you confirm PO cadence, Ben and I will adjust the invoice scheduling to align with your quarter close.
- Kimberly (cc): if Legal has any immediate redline guidance on the tax gross-up or SLA credit language, please flag.

Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: pricing stitch, invoice entity mapping & net-terms proposal

Hi all —

Thanks for the context. A few legal points and proposed language to resolve the open items:

1) Governing precedence: MSA governs, but an Order Form may modify payment terms only if it expressly states so in Section 1.4. I suggest we add a single sentence in the Order Form that states: "Notwithstanding the MSA, the payment terms set forth in this Order Form (Net45 for recurring invoices; Net30 for activation fees) shall apply to invoices issued under this Order Form."

2) Tax responsibility / withholding: instead of a gross-up on all withholding, propose this compromise clause: "Customer is responsible for any taxes assessed on Customer's receipt of Services. If applicable withholding taxes are imposed by a taxing authority on payments to Redwood, the parties will cooperate to minimize double taxation. Should Customer fail to provide valid tax documentation within 30 days of request, Redwood may withhold an amount equal to the tax and invoice Customer net of such withholding; Redwood will provide supporting evidence and will reasonably cooperate on refund or credit adjustments."

3) SLA credit for late payments: acceptable to offer a 5% credit applied to the next invoice if invoices remain unpaid after 60 days, capped at two invoice cycles. I recommend we insert a short billing appendix that enumerates PO requirements and the credit path.

4) Evidence: please attach signed VAT certificates (or W-8/W-9 forms) and clarify which entity will issue PO numbers. Redwood will not recognize net-term changes unless PO lifecycle and entity ownership are confirmed.

Once we have the VAT docs and PO cadence from Oliver, Legal is comfortable finalizing the Order Form with the language above and sending to DocuSign. Naomi / Ben — happy to join a quick 15-min call with Medivex Procurement if that helps expedite.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
